comments.note: Confirmed: workflow-rework-loop.test.ts describe block at line 245 reads 'QA/Reviewer next-action returns WAIT on FAIL (no self-rework)' and individual it() strings at lines 282 and 295 say 'returns WAIT'. The actual assertions now correctly expect WAIT_FOR_REWORK, so the expectations pass, but the description text is stale and will mislead future developers reading the test suite. This should be addressed: rename the describe block and it() strings to reference WAIT_FOR_REWORK.

priorQaPipelines is computed once before P4 and reused at P6. This is an efficient pattern. The auto_cancelled guard (!p.auto_cancelled) is consistently applied in priorQaPipelines, priorReviewPipelines, hasImplPass, and hasQaPass. No drift found.

getQaAction and getReviewerAction share near-identical 7+1b priority loop structures differing only in pipeline type strings and upstream check parameters. The Developer already flagged this (~60 lines of deduplication possible via a shared generic function). This is a valid future refactor with no impact on correctness now; recommend addressing in a dedicated refactor WP when all agent actions are in their final form.

Reviewer P1b uses a local limitedType variable to identify which upstream rework count triggers the limit, which is included in the WAIT_FOR_UPSTREAM_REWORK_LIMIT reason string. This is a nice UX touch. One edge case: if both implementation AND qa reach MAX simultaneously, only 'implementation' is reported (since the ternary short-circuits on the first true condition). Both would trigger P1b anyway since returning on first match, but the reason text would not mention qa. Non-blocking; documenting for awareness.
